Rules

Sporting rules common to all ACC races. Event-specific details appear on its page.

GOOGLE DRIVE / BRIEFINGS

Official event briefings

Review the complete documents and format-specific instructions before joining the track.

Open the briefings ↗
01 / ACC

Driving standards

Race respectfully and predictably. Avoidable contact, dangerous line changes, deliberate braking and unsporting moves are prohibited.

02 / ACC

Start and first corner

Adjust braking for traffic and respect cars alongside. A deliberate collision may lead to immediate disqualification.

03 / ACC

Race control

After a multi-car crash in the first three corners, race control may order one restart. A VSC message then requires the pit limiter and a maximum speed of 50 km/h.

04 / ACC

WGT Sprint

Two drivers per crew for 60 minutes. One stop with a driver change is required. Tyres and fuel are optional.

05 / ACC

WGT Endurance

Crews of 1 to 6 drivers. Each stint is limited to 45 minutes; tyre and fuel strategy is up to the crew.

06 / ACC

Daily Race

A 60-minute race and one real mandatory stop. Tyres and fuel are optional.

07 / ACC

Ballade ATX

A 90-minute race with two real mandatory stops. Tyres and fuel are optional.

08 / ACC

After an incident

Rejoin only when safe and respect blue flags. Submit protests via the event’s SimGrid procedure.

09 / ACC

Registration and results

Maximum 28 drivers; ATXRACING reserves at least one technical slot for the steward. Results become official after incidents have been reviewed.

10 / ACC

Late penalties

A Drive Through imposed too late to serve converts to 30 seconds. Serious incidents may justify a higher penalty; insufficient evidence means no penalty.
